title: 11.5 A 200MHz-BW Blocker-Tolerant Receiver with Fifth-Order Filtering Achieving 19dBm Adjacent-Channel IIP3
problem: 5G NR receivers with 200+ MHz channel bandwidth must handle strong in-band and adjacent-channel blockers while maintaining low noise figure and acceptable power consumption, requiring aggressive analog filtering before digitization.
method: The receiver employs a fifth-order filtering architecture, likely using mixer-first topology with baseband input impedance (Z_BB) exhibiting steep roll-off greater than 20dB/dec. This provides sharp nearby filtering at the RX input while maintaining passive gain through capacitor stacking, carefully trading off noise figure against power consumption.

title: Mint: Cost-Efficient Tracing with All Requests Collection via Commonality and Variability Analysis
problem: Distributed tracing systems face a fundamental tension between preserving essential trace information and reducing the massive volume of traces generated in production. The prevailing '1 or 0' binary sampling strategy either retains a full trace or discards it entirely, which fails to efficiently capture structural commonality across traces while still recording meaningful variability.
method: Mint decomposes traces into a commonality skeleton shared across structurally similar requests and per-request variability deltas that capture deviations. It collects all requests but stores only the variability delta relative to the common template, reducing storage volume while preserving full per-request observability. A commonality and variability analysis pass extracts templates offline or incrementally from the trace stream.

title: REMU: Memory-aware Radiation Emulation via Dual Addressing for In-orbit Deep Learning System
problem: COTS GPUs deployed in space face radiation-induced memory errors but lack effective tools to link radiation faults to runtime DNN behavior; existing emulation methods fail to map errors from physical memory to DNN execution.
method: REMU introduces dual addressing mechanism across virtual, physical, and DRAM memory spaces to precisely map radiation-induced errors from DRAM to runtime DNN inference, enabling efficient error injection and behavioral analysis.

title: ClosureX: Compiler Support for Correct Persistent Fuzzing
problem: Persistent fuzzing reuses a single process across multiple test cases to eliminate process creation/teardown overhead, but process state changes from one test case (heap state, file descriptors, global variables, etc.) persist into subsequent test cases, causing semantic inconsistencies that lead to missed crashes, false crashes, and overall incorrectness in fuzzer-discovered bugs.
method: ClosureX is a compiler pass that identifies and instruments program state that changes during execution and must be restored between fuzzing iterations to maintain semantic consistency. The compiler analyzes the program to determine which state variables are 'closure' — the minimal set that must be reset to restore execution semantics to the pre-iteration state. ClosureX instruments the loop-back path of the persistent fuzzing harness to snapshot this closure state before each test case and restore it before the next, without requiring full process re-initialization. The compiler selects the granularity of state capture (stack, heap allocations, global variables) based on static analysis of reachable effects.

title: DANN: Diffractive Acoustic Neural Network for in-sensor computing system target at multi-biomarker diagnosis
problem: Deploying diffractive neural networks on integrated acoustic (surface acoustic wave) systems for analog edge AI is challenging due to hardware optimization constraints and training complexity. Existing diffractive DNN implementations focus on optical systems; acoustic realizations require novel training and optimization methods.
method: The work applies diffractive neural network algorithms to surface acoustic wave (SAW) systems and introduces a co-training methodology combining Finite Element Analysis (FEA) simulations with gradient-descent optimization. This balances physical realism (FEA) with training efficiency (backprop) to learn diffractive patterns optimized for SAW hardware.

title: MIA-aware FinFlex Cell Legalization with Power-Driven Cell Version Substitution
problem: Standard cell legalization and placement optimization for TSMC FinFlex technology in sub-3nm nodes, accounting for multiple cell versions with varying heights and threshold voltages while respecting minimum implant area (MIA) constraints.
method: Three-stage algorithm: (1) intra-row violation-aware preprocessing considering timing and power; (2) directed acyclic graph (DAG) based initial legalization with cell version substitution; (3) dynamic programming-based inter-row violation removal to handle MIA constraint violations.

title: GPUs All Grown-Up: Fully Device-Driven SpMV Using GPU Work Graphs
problem: Sparse matrix-vector multiplication (SpMV) on GPUs requires expensive host-side preprocessing to select per-row algorithms based on non-zero distribution, forcing costly CPU-GPU round-trips and limiting cache locality. This preprocessing adds latency that is particularly problematic for iterative solvers with repeated SpMV calls.
method: The paper leverages GPU Work Graphs, a novel GPU programming model originally designed for graphics, to implement fully device-driven SpMV self-scheduling. Work Graphs enable fine-grained dataflow execution of individual workgroups using emerging GPU hardware and firmware support (AMD GPUs with rocSPARSE stack). Preprocessing is fused with per-row computation: as soon as preprocessing generates sufficient work metadata, workgroups of specialized per-row SpMV kernels are self-scheduled and dispatched on-device without host interaction. This interleaving improves L1/L2 cache locality and eliminates CPU-GPU synchronization entirely. The approach uses a fixed 25 MiB device-side supporting data structure independent of matrix size, contrasting with scaling structures in rocSPARSE LRB.

title: Concerto: Automatic Communication Optimization and Scheduling for Large-Scale Deep Learning
problem: In large-scale distributed DNN training, collective communication (all-reduce, all-gather, etc.) remains a major bottleneck that existing frameworks address only through hand-crafted, framework-specific overlap strategies tightly coupled to particular parallelism schemes. There is no general, automatic mechanism to overlap computation and communication across arbitrary parallelism configurations.
method: Concerto is a compiler framework that decouples communication optimization from the parallelism strategy. It formulates communication scheduling as a resource-constrained project scheduling problem (RCPSP) and applies an off-the-shelf solver to find near-optimal schedules. An auto-decomposition pass splits synchronous (critical-path) communication operations to create overlap opportunities with computation, without requiring manual annotation. The resulting schedule is emitted as a program that any parallelism backend can execute.

title: 14.5 A 28nm 192.3TFLOPS/W Accurate/Approximate Dual-Mode-Transpose Digital 6T-SRAM CIM Macro for Floating-Point Edge Training and Inference
problem: SRAM CIM macros focus primarily on inference; on-device training requires backpropagation with transposed weights but prior T-CIM designs waste area (separate FF/BP circuits), use low-precision integer formats (accuracy loss), or rely on analog CIM (PVT sensitivity). Fine-tuning accuracy directly impacts user experience.
method: 28nm digital SRAM CIM macro with dual-mode transpose architecture enabling both feed-forward (FF) and backpropagation (BP) via single set of MAC circuits (high reuse). Floating-point (FP) format preserves training accuracy. Approximate computing mode boosts speed/efficiency.

title: UPVSS: Jointly Managing Vector Similarity Search with Near-Memory Processing Systems
problem: Vector similarity search is bandwidth-bound in CPU-based systems; DRAM bandwidth becomes the critical bottleneck as data scales, limiting throughput in recommendation systems and LLM deployments.
method: Offloads similarity search to UPMEM near-memory processing units, distributing computation close to data to reduce core-to-memory data movement and maximize UPMEM's parallelism through architecture-aware workload distribution.

title: Clearwater Forest the Next Generation Intel® Xeon® Processor with Efficiency Cores
problem: Multi-core Xeon processors need improved power efficiency and performance balance across diverse workloads.
method: Intel's Clearwater Forest design integrates efficiency cores alongside performance cores, enabling flexible power management and task scheduling across heterogeneous execution units.

title: HYTE: Flexible Tiling for Sparse Accelerators via Hybrid Static-Dynamic Approaches
problem: Tiling very large sparse tensors on specialized hardware accelerators is challenged by the inability of purely static schemes (which use simple heuristics without adapting to local sparsity patterns) and purely dynamic schemes (which have high design complexity) to jointly find near-optimal tile size/shape, dimension iteration order, buffer allocation, and metadata management while accommodating highly varying local data sparsity.
method: HYTE is a hybrid static-dynamic tiling framework for sparse accelerators. An offline static scheduler first samples the sparse matrix to estimate a near-optimal initial tiling configuration — covering tile size and shape, dimension iteration order across tiles, and buffer allocation policies — without analyzing the full tensor. At runtime, a dynamic tuning mechanism adjusts tile shape on-the-fly to maintain high buffer utilization as local sparsity patterns vary. HYTE also manages tiling metadata in both off-chip memory and on-chip buffer efficiently, handling the non-negligible metadata overhead that prior sparse tiling schemes neglect.

title: EdgeMM: Multi-Core CPU with Heterogeneous AI-Extension and Activation-aware Weight Pruning for Multimodal LLMs at Edge
problem: Multimodal LLMs combine compute-intensive modality encoders with memory-bound LLM decoders, presenting distinct performance bottlenecks that homogeneous CPU designs cannot address efficiently.
method: EdgeMM uses multi-core CPU with heterogeneous AI coprocessors: compute-centric systolic arrays for encoders and memory-centric digital compute-in-memory (CIM) for decoders. Dynamic activation-aware weight pruning and bandwidth management optimize efficiency. Implemented in 22nm commercial technology.

title: Chameleon-SAT: An Adaptive Boolean Satisfiability Accelerator Using Mixed-Signal In-Memory Computing for Versatile SAT Problems
problem: Boolean satisfiability (SAT) problems have diverse scales and complexity; existing SAT solvers cannot efficiently handle the full spectrum with variable solution requirements (completeness, speed).
method: Chameleon-SAT is an ASIC-based SAT accelerator leveraging mixed-signal in-memory computing to support three algorithm classes: local search, Davis-Putnam-Logemann-Loveland (DPLL), and Conflict-Driven Clause Learning (CDCL). Reconfiguration modes allow algorithm selection based on problem characteristics, enabling efficient handling of small-scale high-complexity cases, medium-scale structured cases, and large-scale high-complexity problems.

title: SoMa: Identifying, Exploring, and Understanding the DRAM Communication Scheduling Space for DNN Accelerators
problem: As on-chip buffers on DNN accelerators grow large enough to hold most single-layer weights, single-layer dataflow optimization no longer meaningfully reduces DRAM bandwidth pressure. Multi-layer fusion and DRAM communication scheduling (timing of prefetches and stores across fused layers) remain an open, poorly-characterized optimization problem.
method: SoMa introduces a Tensor-centric Notation (TCN) to formally represent and enumerate DRAM communication scheduling schemes across fused layer groups. An end-to-end scheduling compiler framework explores this space jointly optimizing prefetch timing, data store scheduling, and layer fusion decisions for diverse accelerators and workloads. SoMa has been deployed as a compiler for a commercial accelerator product.

title: InterConFuzz: A Fuzzing-based Comprehensive NoC Verification Framework
problem: Security verification of Network-on-Chip (NoC) systems is challenging due to intricate high-concurrency structures; traditional verification methods fail to achieve comprehensive coverage, leading to prolonged verification and overlooked security vulnerabilities.
method: InterConFuzz is a hybrid hardware fuzzing technique using symbolic execution for extensive coverage of NoC state space. Built on Universal Verification Methodology (UVM) for standard verification flow integration. Applies fuzzing to systematically explore NoC behaviors and identify security flaws in high-concurrency scenarios.
